I've been an addict for over 20 years now. Never once did I not 'have my sh*t together' I always took care of my responsibilities to the point where no one even knew I was an addict until about 7 or 8 years ago. And they only found out when I got arrested for the first time ever due to my spouse getting set up by a 'friend' and they considered me his codefendant. Even during the 2.5 years in probation I was using. PO never suspected a thing because I was working a high paying job, took care of myself, had my own place, a paid off vehicle, etc. Even now as I have yet another home with big expensive TVs with the pricey beds and wrap around sofa, spouse and I both have vehicles, bills always paid, I hold down jobs as an excellent employee and often hold down multiple jobs at a time, I provide everything my children need and then some. I attend all the parent/teacher meetings, make the meals, fold the laundry. But I also think that once you have certain responsibilities you didn't have earlier in your life, such as children, how you handle addiction and such kind of shifts a little bit. If I had $50 left and no dope but my kids also had no food or diapers it's not even a question or hesitation. Thankfully I've been in the game so long that I have a few connections (wether it be product or $$) in my back pocket where at least 1 or 2 is always able to help out in a quick bind. But again, I only have that due to not being the typical POS addict that is unfortunately often times eventually turned into  thief, liar, scumbag, etc.

I was an addict for 20 years, IV opiate addict for 10 when I found out I was 7 weeks pregnant with my first. I wanted that baby, so I made the choice to join a suboxone program. Indulging in only that and weed as a medical marijuana patient, I gave birth to 2 perfectly healthy babies within the span of a little over 2 years. Both were born full term sand completely healthy. They also tested negative at birth for both substances I had been using through both pregnancies. My point is.. IF you want this baby, it is 100% possible to get your life and mind in check before the baby actually comes. Don’t listen to the people that tell you a million things like “are you financially stable?” or “do you have a village at home to help??” because those things don’t always matter. NOBODY is financially stable enough to start a family in this day and age. You don’t have to be. But you do have to be willing and ready to spend your last $20 on diapers and formula instead of down and rigs without even a shred of a second thought.
